title: BRCGS Food Safety Issue 9 – the system in practice
subtitle: Leadership · HACCP · management system · site · product · process · people · audit
note: Original QA Support material. It does not replace the official text of the standard or BRCGS-licensed training. Before an audit, use the current publication and position statements.
footer: TR-001 · BRCGS Food Safety Issue 9 · QA Support

slides.title: Learning objectives
bullets: Explain what BRCGS Food Safety is and how certification works
Know the structure of the standard and fundamental requirements
Understand the role of senior management and food safety culture
Identify evidence of implementation for key requirements
Know non-conformity classification and grades
Prepare the site and team for the audit

slides.title: What BRCGS Food Safety is
bullets: International standard for food manufacturers, GFSI-benchmarked
Required by many retailers and in export markets
Issue 9: published August 2022, audits since February 2023
Supplemented by position statements
Next issue in preparation – always check which version applies

slides.title: Structure of the standard
table: Senior management commitment, food safety culture
Management system: documents, audits, suppliers, CAPA, traceability, recalls
Site standards: layout, fabric, utilities, foreign bodies, hygiene, pests, storage
Product control: development, labels, allergens, authenticity, testing, release
Process control: operations, line label checks, quantity, calibration
Personnel: training, hygiene, medical screening, clothing

slides.title: Fundamental requirements
bullets: Serious failure usually prevents certification
They include, among others:
senior management commitment and continual improvement, HACCP plan
internal audits, management of raw material and packaging suppliers
CAPA, traceability, layout and product flow, housekeeping and hygiene
allergens, control of operations, training
slides.callout: Check the list in the current text of the standard

slides.title: Senior management commitment – evidence
table: at least annually, data and decisions

slides.title: HACCP plan – what the auditor looks at
bullets: Competent, multidisciplinary HACCP team
Complete flow diagrams confirmed on the floor
Hazard analysis: B, C, P, allergens + link to food defence and authenticity
Justified CCPs and validated critical limits
Monitoring and corrective actions – on the floor and in records
Plan verified and reviewed at least annually and after changes

slides.title: Exercise 1 – culture by numbers
bullets: Propose 3 measurable food safety culture indicators
Add one action for the next 6 months to each
Example indicators:
number of staff reports per month
culture survey score year on year
% of management walkabouts completed as planned

slides.title: Key areas of section 3
table: programme on ≥ 4 dates per year, independent auditors
risk assessment of each material, monitoring
rework and packaging missing from test

slides.title: Incidents and recalls
bullets: Procedure and crisis team with 24/7 contacts
Procedure tested at least annually
Authority notified when product may be unsafe (Art. 19 Reg. 178/2002)
Certification body notified of a recall: 3 working days
Final report and lessons into CAPA

slides.title: Exercise 2 – traceability test
bullets: Choose a product from last week
In 20 minutes list the documents needed to establish:
raw material, packaging and rework batches
process parameters and CCP records
quantities produced, dispatched, in stock
customers
Mark where the chain could break
slides.callout: Practical target: full data within 4 hours

slides.title: Section 4 – key questions
table: Who has access? Are vulnerable points protected?
Do dirty and clean routes avoid crossing?
Are surfaces in good condition? Are water and air controlled?
Is there hygiene clearance after work?
Glass register, knives, detectors and testing?

slides.title: Production risk zones (section 8)
bullets: Zones: low risk, high care, high risk, ambient high care
Physical segregation and controlled entry
Clothing and footwear change, hand washing and sanitising
Filtered air at appropriate pressure
Dedicated equipment and tools
Environmental monitoring programme (Listeria)

slides.title: Product control (section 5)
table: legal and recipe compliance, change approval
risk assessment, segregation, cleaning validation, justified warnings
vulnerability assessment, claim documents, mass balance

slides.title: Process and personnel (sections 6–7)
bullets: Process specifications, protected equipment settings
Label and packaging checks at start-up and product change
Net quantity control, calibration of critical instruments
Training before starting work and competence assessment (incl. agency)
Personal hygiene, illness reporting, visitors, protective clothing

slides.title: Audit process
table: certification body, scope, date or unannounced option
a large part of the audit is in production

slides.title: Non-conformities and grades
table: 11–16 minors or 1 major + up to 10 minors
17–24 minors or 1 major + 11–16 or 2 majors + up to 10
critical or more than for D
slides.callout: Unannounced audit: grade with '+', e.g. AA+

slides.title: Preparation – 10 points
bullets: Internal audits of all sections, ≥ 4 dates per year
Previous non-conformities closed with evidence of effectiveness
HACCP review, traceability and recall tests (≤ 12 months)
Management review with current data
Current risk assessments: materials, allergens, food defence, authenticity
Culture plan with evidence, skills matrix
GMP inspection one week before, auditor guide

slides.title: Final exercise – from risk to evidence
slides.callout: Next: final test – 15 questions, pass mark 80%

slides.title: Summary
bullets: BRCGS assesses whether the system works on the floor – not only on paper
Leadership and culture are requirements, not extras
Fundamental requirements = implementation priority
Every requirement needs evidence: record, observation, interview
A non-conformity is information – root cause and effectiveness matter
